diagrams.title: Before: one regional runtime
diagrams.description: Existing runtime, current policy, governed model lineage and saved operations live in one logical regional deployment.

diagrams.title: After: regional cells with an EU authority quorum
diagrams.description: Placement binds Tenant C to the US hostname and A/B to the EU hostname, whose TLS ends only in EU ingress. An EU-only 2-of-3 authority quorum holds policy, approvals, tombstones and the writer lease. EU-primary replicates asynchronously to EU-secondary. On primary loss the promotion gate either passes every check or fails closed.

diagrams.title: Recovery sequence: control plane, then data plane
diagrams.description: The incident controller detects, places, fences and restores without talking to the client. Fencing waits for lease expiry, installs epoch 8 in the stores EU-secondary will use, probes epoch 7 and quarantines EU-primary's stores. Alice's request then reaches EU ingress through the EU hostname before admission and reconciliation. Failed prerequisites stop promotion.

lab_assumptions: Toy policy: A/B allowed in EU only, RPO 60 seconds, RTO 600 seconds, 20-second lease. Loss bound = gap at isolation + lease. The plan is detection 60 + fencing 30 + restore + route 30 + validation 60 seconds. Safety gates decide promotion; a plan over the RTO is a separate planning miss to rehearse or redesign, not a block. Policy, approval, audit and bundle gates are assumed true here; Python tests exercise them. Results are computed from assumptions, not measured.
